recognize_zh: 鐵染色（Prussian blue）下，一顆被紅色核染劑染成粉紅的紅血球母細胞核，周圍環繞一圈藍綠色的鐵顆粒、排列在核的外圍，形成環狀，這就是環狀鐵粒母細胞（ring sideroblast）；影像失焦、解析度有限。
features: Single erythroid precursor nucleus stained pink-red by the counterstain
Blue siderotic granules arranged around the nuclear perimeter in a ring-like distribution
Granules encircle most of the nuclear circumference
Few scattered free iron granules in the adjacent background
Image is out of focus, limiting granule counting and assessment of cytoplasmic outline
describe_en: Iron-stained bone marrow aspirate smear (Prussian blue with a red nuclear counterstain) shows an erythroid precursor with multiple blue siderotic granules arranged in a perinuclear ring encircling most of the nucleus. The image is blurred, so the exact number of granules and the proportion of the circumference involved cannot be precisely assessed. Findings are consistent with a ring sideroblast (conventionally at least 5 granules covering at least one third of the nuclear circumference).

ddx.vs: Normal sideroblasts contain only 1–4 small scattered cytoplasmic granules that are not arranged around the nucleus.
Storage iron lies in macrophages as coarse clumps or diffuse blue cytoplasm and is not organized as a perinuclear ring within an erythroblast.
Pappenheimer bodies are small iron granules in anucleate red cells, without a surrounding nucleus.
